name: open
description: Open a Bitbucket Cloud pull request. Defaults to the branch the workspace is on, against the repository's own main branch. The branch must already be pushed: nothing in these packs pushes for you.

body.description: The description, as markdown. Sent as Bitbucket's `description` field; the parameter is named `body` so a flow can swap this tool for the github one unchanged.

source.description: The branch to merge from. Omit to use the branch the workspace is on.

target.description: The branch to merge into. Omit to use the repository's own main branch, which is read from the API rather than assumed.

repo.description: The repository as "workspace/repository". Omit to read it from the origin remote.

output_schema.description: The pull request that was opened. `number` and `url` are what a later step needs. `draft` is reported and cannot be asked for: the github pack takes a draft parameter and this one does not, which is the single place the two open tools differ.

exit_codes.0: success (the new pull request is on stdout as JSON)
exit_codes.2: invalid input (title is missing, a parameter is wrong, or source and target are the same branch)
exit_codes.4: not permitted (the git repository is above the workspace root)
exit_codes.5: unreachable (DNS failure, connection refused, TLS failure, or the transfer timed out)
exit_codes.6: http error (the API refused: the branch is not pushed, a pull request is already open for it, or the token was refused)
exit_codes.7: no credential (BITBUCKET_TOKEN is not in this step's environment)
